name: DaVatta Incorporated

tenures.role: stable — entrance music 'Got Yourself a Gun' by Nas featuring Scarface
tenures.source: OSF's own stable, tag team and roster-card pages and the dated posts naming it

caption: OSF's heel mob stable out of Chicago, owner Junior DaVatta's Italian henchmen, which ran the Fighting Division's front office and sent Anthony DaVatta and Frank Scarpo out as its tag team.

name: The Clan

tenures.role: stable — eight ninjas lettered A to H on its card, one of them named Ichiharu
tenures.source: OSF's own stable, tag team and roster-card pages and the dated posts naming it

caption: A stable of ninjas billed from Miami via Kyoto, allied to Inphino Blitz, who fought Kenyatta Jackson in a best-of-seven series and vanished from the cage after each loss.

identity.note: A shared stable name only; the held records are an LCW stable of 1997 and a NEWF stable, and no document names either with this one.

name: Blue Dragons

tenures.source: OSF's own stable, tag team and roster-card pages and the dated posts naming it

caption: The Kitagami brothers from Sado Island, Japan, whose tag team split in May 2003 when Hiro was injured and reported kidnapped and who ended up brawling through a Chicago hospital in July.

name: Holy Underground

tenures.role: team — named in the B3 review only
tenures.source: The 7 October 2003 president's review of B3, which names it once

caption: A team that beat DaVatta Incorporated at B3 and is named in the president's column with no member list.

identity.note: A shared team name in one year only. PWC's Holy Underground (May-June 2003) is the Irish tag team Limerick and Caleb McGlocklan, feuding with the preacher Eric Sagar's Revival (/promotions/pwc-wrestleonline-2003/archive/pwc-wrestleonline-2003-pwc-tv-2003-05-17.html); OSF's Holy Underground is named once, beating DaVatta Incorporated at the Chicago fighting federation's B3, in the president's review of 7 October 2003 (/promotions/osf-2003/archive/presidents-review-b3-2003-10-07.html), with no member named; neither member appears in any OSF document. Pending a verdict: reopenable if an OSF card names its members.
